case_name: Sou Ruta Sanjay Karkhanis vs Sanjay Surendra Karkhanis
facts_of_case: The wife challenged the decree passed by the Family Court granting judicial separation in favour of the husband. The parties got married in 1985 and had a male issue in 1987. The wife left her parents' place after police intervention.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion requires two essential conditions: factum of separation and intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.
legal_principles.held: For the offence of desertion, so far as the deserting spouse is concerned, two essential conditions must be there, namely, (1) the factum of separation, and (2) the intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end (animus deserendi).

legal_principles.principle: Desertion comes to an end if the deserted spouse affirms the marriage and is ready and willing to resume married life.
legal_principles.held: Hence, it is necessary that during all the period that there has been a desertion, the deserted spouse must affirm the marriage and be ready and willing to resume married life on such conditions as may be reasonable.

legal_principles.principle: A party claiming divorce on the ground of desertion must prove that it was ready to cohabit throughout the said period.
legal_principles.held: Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act requires that a party claiming divorce on the ground of desertion should prove that it was ready to cohabit throughout the said period of 2 years prior to the filing of the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming divorce to prove that it was ready to cohabit throughout the said period.
The law relating to desertion is well settled by the Apex Court.

outcome.final_order: The final court order granted decree for judicial separation in favour of the husband.
